posts.title: Tennis Auckland unveils new clubhouse, roof details ahead of 2027 ASB Classic
posts.description: Enjoy the sight of people mopping up centre court with tablecloths while you still can. That was Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown’s advice at Thursday night’s First Serve event to kick off the countdown to the 2027 ASB Classic . January’s tournament should be the last without a roof over Manuka Doctor Arena. Meanwhile, event hosts Tennis Auckland unveiled a new clubhouse. But tennis isn’t the only game in town. At the Stanley Street Clubhouse official opening that same evening, the sports on offer were pickleball and golf. Amid the bubbles and Aperol spritzes, prawns tucked into crackers and little fish sliders, guests could pick up a paddle or try their swing in a golf simulator. Tennis Auckland’s newest sports facility The clubhouse started with a very different objective. Tennis Auckland rented the University of Auckland’s old gym to give ASB Classic players more room during the tournament. The players liked it. posts.title: NZ firm Huski shrugs off global IP stoush, $2m heist to create world-first coffee cup design
posts.description: A New Zealand firm that spent five years in an IP stoush which pitted it against a $1.4 billion global packaging giant before losing a $2.1 million export shipment in a major UK cargo heist, has now developed a world-first coffee cup design. Auckland-based Huski says it spent hundreds of thousands of dollars defending its brand before reaching an agreement that restricted its ability to sell coffee and other hot drink products under the Huski name. The dispute intensified after the opposing business was acquired by a much larger multinational packaging group, leaving the privately owned New Zealand company facing the prospect of significantly higher legal costs. Prolonged legal and IP dispute Huski co-founder Simon Huesser says the company eventually had to make a commercial decision about how long it could continue the fight. posts.title: Josiah Morgan named as 2027 Emerging Māori Writer in residence
posts.description: Josiah Morgan has been appointed the 2027 Emerging Māori Writer in Residence. The residency is jointly offered by Te Herenga Waka – Victoria University of Wellington ’s International Institute of Modern Letters (IIML) and Creative New Zealand. Morgan’s publications in Aotearoa include i’m still growing (Dead Bird Books) and Black Window (featured poet selection, Poetry Aotearoa Yearbook 2026). His writing has also received recognition internationally. His novella Road: A Postlapsarian Comedywon the Macmillan Brown Prize in 2021. In 2026, he was a visiting writer at Washington State University, where he celebrated the republication of his book The Texas Chainsaw Massacre with Index Press. Beyond writing, Morgan has worked as a creative producer for Tiny Fest and programme manager for Te Wā The Space.
